name: Eurocommunism
summary: Eurocommunism was the 1970s current in the Western European communist parties, above all the Italian, Spanish and briefly French, that sought socialism through peaceful democratic means. It accepted a multi-party system, free speech and alternation in power, dropped the dictatorship of the proletariat and Leninist state-smashing, and asserted independence from Moscow. Its economy was a long-run mixed one, with public and private property side by side, pursued through broad alliances including Catholics.
scope: The mainstream of the PCI under Enrico Berlinguer and the PCE under Santiago Carrillo, 1968 to the early 1980s, drawing on Gramsci; based on Berlinguer's 1977 Moscow speech and related statements, Carrillo's Eurocommunism and the State, and the 1975 and 1977 joint declarations. It excludes the French PCF's brief and hesitant turn, Marxism-Leninism, and later social-democratic successors.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The PCI and PCE backed expanded public social services as part of a democratic road to socialism, and Italy's national health service of 1978 was a PCI-supported reform.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not a theme in the sources; inferred from the parties' labour-movement base and wage-bargaining politics, though Berlinguer also urged wage moderation in 1970s austerity.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Carrillo wanted democratic control of a mixed economy and saw the capitalist economy as the structural source of state subordination, so adherents reject market supremacy.

public-ownership.rationale: Carrillo backed public ownership of key sectors but alongside private property 'for a long period', so a firm but not absolute yes.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian aims and Berlinguer's call that austerity not fall on workers; no tax programme was read.

unions-good.rationale: The parties were rooted in the labour movement and sought alliances of labour and culture; unions are core allies in the strategy.

property-fundamental.rationale: Carrillo accepted private property and initiative for a long period but within a socialist transformation, so it is not a fundamental right overriding collective aims.

regulate-corporations.rationale: A democratically steered mixed economy implies tighter public control of corporations, though Carrillo even allowed multinationals in nationally useful sectors.

cut-welfare.rationale: Eurocommunist parties defended and extended the welfare state, and Berlinguer's austerity was framed as fairer, not as cuts to workers.

worker-ownership.rationale: Self-management appeared in some Eurocommunist debate but the sources stress a coexistence of public and private property rather than worker-owned firms; split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to civil liberties; the PCI also backed tough anti-terror measures in the 1970s, so confidence is low.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the parties differed and mostly avoided the question.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; free speech commitments pull one way, antifascist tradition the other.

strong-leader.rationale: Eurocommunism defined itself against Stalinist personal rule and committed to pluralism and alternation in power.

state-harmful.rationale: Carrillo wanted to democratise and use the state as a tool for socialism, not abolish it.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the left European norm; no source states a position.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred; Carrillo urged winning over the army and a national-defence army rather than bigger repressive forces, and the PCI also supported order in the 1970s.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; Eurocommunist parties engaged feminism but left no clear stance on this.

decide-locally.rationale: The parties were national in strategy; the PCI supported regional government in Italy but this is not central.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the humanist left tradition and constitutional approach; not stated in the sources.

traditional-family.rationale: The parties engaged feminism and gay liberation and helped pass Italy's divorce law, defending it in the 1974 referendum.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The parties engaged gay liberation, but marriage equality came later; inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: The PCI and allied left backed legal abortion in Italy in the 1970s as part of engaging feminism.

more-religion-public.rationale: Berlinguer wanted a secular state, neither theist, atheist nor anti-theist, though he courted Catholics; so against a larger public religious role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian principles; the sources do not discuss historical racial injustices.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; the parties engaged feminism without a stated view on this theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Eurocommunists stressed national roads to socialism and Gramscian national-popular culture, yet critics note they rarely stressed tradition; split.

gradual-change.rationale: Their strategy was a peaceful 'march toward socialism' through winning hegemony, but aimed at deep transformation, not respect for existing institutions as such.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from internationalist left stance; not discussed in the sources.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed directly; Carrillo stressed not destabilising the world balance and the PCI favoured detente and European institutions.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred; the parties favoured a state-guided mixed economy, though the PCI turned pro-European and accepted the common market.

nation-first.rationale: Eurocommunism stressed national roads to socialism but also European cooperation and detente; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; the parties stressed non-intervention and detente.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from internationalism tempered by the practical politics of Western European parties; no stated view.

limit-growth.rationale: Berlinguer's 1977 austerity speech sought a fairer, more austere society but not an end to growth; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic for the 1970s peak; inferred from state-led planning and austerity ideas.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Carrillo cites science and technique eroding dogma, but no general techno-optimism is stated.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The PCI backed nuclear power in the 1970s then shifted in the 1980s; adherents were split.

revolution-justified.rationale: They explicitly chose a peaceful democratic road; Carrillo wanted to democratise the state without destroying it by force, though revolution was not renounced in principle against dictatorship.

experts-over-public.rationale: Democratic commitment suggests against technocracy; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Carrillo envisaged a long coexistence of public and private forms and criticised Soviet bureaucracy, so full central planning is not endorsed.

socialized-markets.rationale: The mixed economy with public and private property implies markets under social control; not stated as market socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; no position in the sources.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian aims; no source states it.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic for the 1970s peak; the parties favoured universal public services over cash income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; PCI pro-European positions point against, state-guided industry for.

state-directs-investment.rationale: A democratically managed mixed economy implies public steering of investment, a standard aim of the PCI and PCE.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Carrillo defended small private initiative alongside public property, yet no distributist aim is stated.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: They sought long coexistence of public and private forms, not the abolition of wages; abolition remains only a distant Marxist horizon.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Contradicts a state-guided mixed economy; inferred from principles.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Berlinguer's compromise involved bargaining with parties and unions, but not state-run corporatist bodies; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: The defining break with Moscow: a multi-party system, free speech and alternation in power, as in the 1975 Berlinguer-Marchais declaration.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The PCE accepted the Spanish monarchy pragmatically in the 1977-78 transition, but republican tradition remained; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Berlinguer called democracy a historically universal value on which to build socialism.

direct-votes.rationale: They valued representative pluralist democracy plus mass participation; no stance on referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: They sought socialism through the existing pluralist democratic institutions, not councils replacing parliaments.

natural-rulers.rationale: Democratic and egalitarian commitments are incompatible with natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: They renounced violence as strategy in their democratic road, but did not adopt absolute pacifism; Carrillo anticipated army splits.

war-builds-character.rationale: Contradicts detente and peace-oriented politics of the parties; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Berlinguer's 'secular and democratic state, neither theist, atheist nor anti-theist' but he also welcomed believers into the party.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A secular democratic state was the PCI's stated goal.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Contradicts a socialist commitment to public state functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Carrillo said Spain should not destabilise the world balance; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Contrary to internationalist, pluralist outlook; inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxist roots remained, but Carrillo and the PCI stressed alliances and hegemony over sectarian class confrontation.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Egalitarian aims; Berlinguer wanted a less unequal society; not stated as equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The sources never address indigenous land rights, and nothing in their principles settles it.

civilizational-union.rationale: Internationalist and secular outlook opposes unions by religion or civilization; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Collectivist socialist ethics contradict self-interest as the moral basis.

duties-before-rights.rationale: They emphasised democratic liberties as universal value, so rights are not subordinated to duties, even if Berlinguer called for collective sacrifice.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmentalism was not a theme of the peak period.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: They worked within industrial society's labour movement and sought to democratise it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No stated view; their reformist gradualism makes disruption unattractive.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bioenhancement is anachronistic for the 1970s and no source gives a view.

restore-past-order.rationale: Eurocommunism looks forward to a socialist transformation.

direct-action.rationale: Their strategy was elections and parliament plus mass movements within democracy.

means-match-ends.rationale: Democracy as both terrain and foundation of socialism means means and ends are linked, per Berlinguer.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly alien to a Marxist labour movement party.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A distant Marxist aim but not in their programme; they pursued reform.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The classical communist aim, but no source emphasises it in Eurocommunist practice.

production-for-use.rationale: Classical aim, but the mixed economy with private initiative qualifies it.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist analysis was retained, though their strategy was not expressed in these terms.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Carrillo rejected the classical dictatorship of the proletariat model and the PCE dropped it, as suited to when workers were a minority.

collective-farming.rationale: Carrillo recognised private initiative and the PCI defended peasants' small property; Soviet collectivisation was criticised as Stalinist.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist analysis once central, but Eurocommunists stressed detente and peaceful coexistence; split.

taxation-theft.rationale: Incompatible with their commitment to public services.

harm-principle.rationale: Not stated; liberal civil liberties plus socialist aims make for no clear fit.

individual-rights-only.rationale: They stressed social and collective rights alongside democratic liberties; inferred.

conscription.rationale: The PCI accepted national defence; Carrillo called for an army capable of national defence; no position on conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: They centred voting and democratic participation as the check on power.

positive-liberty.rationale: A socialism built on democratic freedoms with material equality implies freedom needs material means; inferred from Berlinguer's democracy and equality combination.

media-academia-power.rationale: They sought a bloc of labour and culture rather than blaming media/academia; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Rejected by Marxist and egalitarian traditions.

organic-representation.rationale: They defended party-based pluralist parliamentary democracy.

total-state.rationale: They broke with the Soviet total-state model in favour of pluralism in social, cultural and ideal life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not a fit; Eurocommunism is a left reform movement.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal principle, incompatible with their democracy.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Gramscian hegemony ideas suggest partial sympathy, but the question is epistemological and unaddressed.

universal-morality.rationale: Berlinguer called democracy a universal value, yet no general moral theory is stated.

single-common-good.rationale: They accepted pluralism of interests and parties; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: PCI and PCE positions varied with the Middle East politics; no firm stance in the sources.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No source on Eurocommunism takes up diaspora return or citizenship claims.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival was not an issue the sources link to Eurocommunism, so no stance is inferable.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Economic democracy and democratic control of firms fit their democratic socialism, though the sources emphasise party and state democracy.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from state-led economy, though Berlinguer backed anti-inflation austerity in the 1970s.

economic-freedom.rationale: They defended political freedom as universal value independently of capitalism; economic freedom claim unstated.

rule-by-example.rationale: Berlinguer's moral question was about honest institutions, but he did not advocate rule by example instead of laws.

national-self-determination.rationale: National roads to socialism; the parties supported national independence; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Berlinguer rejected state atheism and welcomed believers.

class-collaboration.rationale: They sought broad alliances yet remained a class-based party; Berlinguer's compromise was with parties, not employers as partners.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Contrary to Gramscian national-popular cultural engagement.

dominated-front.rationale: They sought independence from Moscow and also from superpower blocs; no anti-Western front.

workers-nation.rationale: Critics like Mandel saw Italian and French parties as nationalist, but the parties kept internationalist language; split leaning no.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Carrillo: the state continues to be an instrument of class domination, hence democratising it.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy supply policy is not covered in the sources; adherents' views are unrecorded.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy theory alien to their politics.

proportional-representation.rationale: The PCI worked under and favoured proportional representation in Italy; Spain's 1977 system was also proportional.

national-mission.rationale: Rejects exporting a model; Eurocommunism rejected Soviet model as universal.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Engagement with feminism implies some acceptance.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from PCE's democratic reconciliation line; note Carrillo pursued Reconciliation and pragmatic compromise in Spain.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Incompatible with welfare and mixed economy.

socialism-one-country.rationale: They pursued national roads to socialism; Berlinguer spoke of a socialism necessary and possible in Italy.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The movement left no documented analysis of settler states in the sources opened.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Secularism and equal citizenship suggest yes; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Secular state; though the PCI compromised with Catholics in Italy.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Rejects Stalinist state-strengthening doctrine and pursued pluralism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Socialism by democratic majorities and alternation in power.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade balance goals are not addressed; the sources are silent on it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Marxist outlook sees progress as collective and class-driven rather than as struggle among individuals and peoples; inferred from Marxist roots.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: PCI defended constitutional order against right extremism but commitment to pluralism pulls against bans.

separated-powers.rationale: Fidelity to democratic institutions and the constitution; Carrillo wanted to democratise the state apparatus rather than replace it.

vanguard-party.rationale: Carrillo's hegemonic bloc of labour and culture and pluralism replaced the Leninist vanguard model.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: British-style housing policy is not covered in the sources; no stance can be inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Defence of democratic liberties as universal value, though the PCI backed firm counter-terror measures in the 1970s.

party-controls-media.rationale: Pluralism of social and cultural life rejects control of information.

party-commands-army.rationale: Carrillo sought a national-defence army, not a party army; pluralism.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from internationalist outlook; the sources do not discuss naturalisation rules.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian ethics; the PCI practice tied party deputies' pay to worker wages historically; low.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Democratic centralism was formally retained by the PCI at times while pluralism and dissent grew; split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The PCI turned pro-European after 1969 and placed Altiero Spinelli on its list.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not a communist concern; Berlinguer only asked for a state neutral toward religion.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Detente and national defence orientation; Berlinguer accepted NATO membership and Carrillo wanted national defence.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is not discussed in the sources; representative democracy was their frame.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Berlinguer wanted Italy to stay in NATO, feeling safer on the Western side.

people-in-arms.rationale: Carrillo wanted professional soldiers won over to the left, not an armed citizenry.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification was not addressed in the sources opened.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Gramscian emphasis on culture and intellectuals within a labour-and-culture bloc.

death-penalty.rationale: Italian and Spanish left opposed capital punishment; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Engagement with feminism and gay liberation.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The sources record no stance on pornography regulation.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from internationalist and egalitarian leanings; not discussed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Spanish PCE supported regional languages; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Berlinguer wanted a neutral secular state but the sources say nothing on exemptions from general law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Cultural nonconformism is not addressed in the sources.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Third-world debt was not a theme in the sources opened.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Colonial independence debates are outside the sources, so no inference is made.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The PCE supported a democratic constituent process for the post-Franco constitution; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presidential election methods are not covered; Berlinguer worked within Italy's parliamentary system.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Carrillo recognised private property and initiative within social goals.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Carrillo called the Soviet state intermediate between the capitalist and authentic socialist state; neither answer.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk policy is anachronistic for the movement's peak and unaddressed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Condemnation of 1968 invasion suggests principle; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Berlinguer courted Catholics and rejected anti-theism.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from democratic commitments; the sources do not discuss secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: No source addresses autonomy within a larger state in these terms.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Eurocommunists kept a Marxist framework and Gramscian strategy while adapting tactics, so they do not put results above ideology; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Berlinguer's 1981 moral question attacked party-system corruption, but the PCI itself governed and defended democratic institutions, so adherents were split on the framing.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not a stated theme; inferred from the Marxist and Gramscian view that consciousness and character are shaped by social conditions and hegemony.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Eurocommunists committed to pluralist democracy, free speech and alternation in power, which rules out a ruler exempt from the law.

space-expansion.rationale: Never addressed; the parties' focus was social reform and democratic transition, so adherents had no settled view.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred: the parties sought rule by the democratic majority through parliament and mass parties, not a constitution balancing few against many.

leader-cult.rationale: The break with the Soviet model included rejecting Stalinist-style personality cults in favour of democratic pluralism and collective party leadership.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the parties' commitment to gender equality and the 1970s family-law reforms they backed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred: the Eurocommunists broke with the Soviet model and its theory of continuing struggle against party leaders, and sought a democratic road with broad alliances.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred: the PCI and PCE came from a tradition backing peasant land reform, but their 1970s mixed-economy line stressed alliances and kept private property, so support is moderate.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from the movement's democratic and human-rights commitments, which favour return of the displaced; the topic was not central.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred: the movement was internationalist and committed to existing democratic states, and gave no support to claims over territory by nationality.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Berlinguer's secular state and the 1975 pledge to civil liberties imply rejecting legal punishment for leaving a religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from the stated commitment to individual freedoms and a secular state; the question was not addressed directly.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred: the PCI backed European integration and direct elections to the European Parliament in the 1970s; a common currency was not itself debated.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred: the movement's national roads to socialism and internationalism did not include ethnic-kin political unions.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: the PCI and PCE backed regional autonomy and cultural rights for minorities within the democratic state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the movement's commitment to democratic struggle within existing states and equal rights under pluralism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Eurocommunism remained Marxist and so gives primacy to the mode of production, though Gramscian stress on culture and hegemony softens it.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred: anti-monopoly policy was a staple of Western communist programmes, within a mixed economy that kept competitive private firms.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred: the parties favoured public intervention and a strong state role to protect jobs rather than letting firms fail.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Berlinguer treated democracy as a universal value including constitutional guarantees and pluralism, which are limits on any single majority.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred: the parties championed women's equality as part of social movements, though quotas were not a stated Eurocommunist position.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred: the movement backed European integration and an open mixed economy, not autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from the movement's labour-based social programme and internationalism.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: the parties pursued a long-run mixed economy that kept material incentives, though Berlinguer's 1970s appeals for austerity stressed social duty.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Eurocommunists took a peaceful, democratic and parliamentary road and rejected insurrectionary and vanguard methods.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred: left republican egalitarianism opposes hereditary privilege, although Carrillo's PCE accepted the monarchy in the 1977 transition.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from its national road to socialism and Gramscian national-popular approach, which rooted communism in each country's own history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from its democratic principles and the left's anti-colonial tradition; no source addresses tutelage directly.

patriotic-education.rationale: Not addressed; it embraced national traditions and independence but also a secular, pluralist state, so adherents had no common line.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian and anti-discrimination commitments; the issue came to the fore in the US only later.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from its programme of public control of key sectors within a mixed economy.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred from Berlinguer's reading of the 1970s crisis as showing capitalism's limits, which required austerity and structural reform.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from its pro-European and anti-imperialist turn, with no claim to influence over the Italian or Spanish imperial past.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from its acceptance of NATO and the European Community; it sought socialism inside Western integration.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred from its broad class alliances and view of workers as one class; the thesis is a Third Worldist one that it did not hold.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from its pluralist democratic commitments and its defence of civil liberties as universal values.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Berlinguer called democracy a historically universal value, and the 1975 declaration pledged guaranteed freedoms, supporting entrenched rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; Eurocommunists were anti-imperialist but the sources discuss no treaty questions.

elective-rulers.rationale: They accepted pluralism, free elections and alternation in power as a core commitment.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from acceptance of majority rule in a multi-party democracy; the sources do not discuss vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to constitutional democracy and rights; not stated in the sources.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Berlinguer and Carrillo accepted parliamentary democracy as the arena for socialism, though with mass movements alongside.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the mainstream European view.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: They sought equality through public provision and class politics, not elite duty; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: As mass parties rooted in the labour movement, they held that politics should be broad participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Gramsci's influence suggests a view of culture reproducing the order; the sources do not state it on mass media.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramsci's hegemony is the intellectual basis of Eurocommunism's strategy of winning cultural consent.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents were split between dependency-style views and social-democratic views.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from internationalist and democratic universalism; not stated.

party-own-road.rationale: Independence from Moscow and a national road to socialism were the defining Eurocommunist claims, as in Berlinguer's 1977 speech.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; the question concerns developing countries.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and acceptance of European post-war order; not stated.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from its universal-suffrage democracy, which rejects rule by descent.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism was the founding experience of the PCI and PCE, which helped write the Italian constitution.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Communists resisted the equivalence thesis, though Eurocommunists did criticize Soviet repression; inferred from that mix.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Marxist historiography treating slavery as the central cause.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; the parties' support for feminist and social movements does not settle it.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the parties' alliance with the feminist movement, which stresses gendered violence.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: They held democracy as a historically universal value (Berlinguer), which contradicts civilization-specific forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Carrillo, who lived through Franco's army, and Berlinguer insisted on civilian democratic control of the military.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from alliances with the women's movement; the sources do not mention it.

filial-duty.rationale: Not a theme in the sources; inferred from the strong family culture of the Italian and Spanish parties, though adherents did not make it doctrine.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to pluralist democracy and elected office; public service entry by examination was not a Eurocommunist theme.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the long-run mixed economy with public ownership of key sectors and planning, which implies national control of strategic firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the PCI and PCE secular, civil-rights outlook and their alliance with the divorce reform side; not stated in the opened sources.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Eurocommunists accepted representative parliamentary democracy with regular elections and alternation in power rather than binding mandates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from support for a public welfare state; private individual accounts in place of state pensions fit neither the mixed economy nor the parties' labour base.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Carrillo accepted a long-run mix of public and private property side by side, so land was not to be held only on condition of use.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary control of the executive and of public money followed from the commitment to a multi-party parliamentary road to socialism.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from pluralism and secular-democratic outlook; the PCE in Spain backed regional languages and autonomy.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from internationalism and the mixed-economy outlook, which did not favour a ban on foreign land purchase.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from the parties' commitment to equality and anti-discrimination; the sources do not address intent versus outcome.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Berlinguer preached austerity in the 1970s and rejected consumer-society values, calling for a different model of development.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Eurocommunists broke with Moscow and opposed Soviet armed meddling; arming foreign insurgents is inferred as contrary to their peaceful, independent line.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Berlinguer told Brezhnev that the 1968 invasion of Czechoslovakia had shown deep differences, and Eurocommunism arose in reaction to the Prague intervention.

missingStatements.text: Parties competing for power should accept alternation in government, giving it up after losing an election.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1975 Berlinguer-Marchais declaration committed to free speech and alternation in power, a founding Eurocommunist pledge.

missingStatements.text: A communist party should be independent of any foreign state or party and follow its own national road to socialism.
missingStatements.rationale: Independence from Moscow and national roads to socialism define the movement after the 1968 invasion.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the communist-party movement and its Soviet ties; too niche to ask of every ideology.

missingStatements.text: A party representing the working class should seek a governing alliance with its main rival, including religious parties, rather than rule alone.
missingStatements.rationale: Berlinguer's historic compromise sought an accord with the Christian Democrats.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the Italian historic compromise; too niche to ask of every ideology.

missingStatements.text: The capitalist state can be democratised and used to build socialism rather than smashed and replaced.
missingStatements.rationale: Carrillo's central thesis in Eurocommunism and the State.

notes: Primary sourcing is partial: Berlinguer quotes come via Wikiquote and Carrillo quotes via a critical review, as the full texts could not be opened. Many answers outside democracy, state, property and the USSR are low-confidence inferences. The French PCF differed on NATO and the nuclear deterrent.
